mainEntity.name: How do sound baths differ from meditation or traditional yoga classes?

acceptedAnswer.text: While sound baths, meditation, and yoga all aim to promote relaxation and well-being, their approaches differ. Sound baths are passive; you simply lie down and receive the sounds and vibrations. Meditation often involves active mental focus, and yoga combines physical postures with breathwork. A key practical tradeoff is that sound baths offer a guided, immersive sensory experience without requiring physical exertion or specific meditation techniques, making them accessible even if you find it challenging to quiet your mind in traditional meditation or yoga.
acceptedAnswer.description: Sound baths are passive, immersive sound experiences for relaxation, unlike active mental focus in meditation or physical postures in yoga. They require no physical exertion.
